chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Samaan said:

I asked him about buying [an item] with deceit and theft, so he said: 'If you know that it is so, then there is no [problem] except if it is something you bought from the agent (tax collector/official).'

key_terms.الْخِيَانَةِ: Deceit, fraud, or treachery in transaction
key_terms.الْعَامِلِ: The agent, tax collector, or official representative of the state/Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying goods known to be acquired through deceit or theft?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling on purchasing goods known to be acquired through deceit (*khiyanah*) or theft (*sariqah*). He establishes that such purchases are generally valid unless the item was bought directly from the government agent (*al-amil*) who collected it, a distinction rooted in the specific legal status of state-collected assets in Shia jurisprudence. This highlights the nuance between private ownership rights and public treasury claims in commercial transactions.
